relations.subject: Penor Rinpoche

relations.subject: Penor Rinpoche
relations.evidence: studying and receiving teachings from numerous masters and scholars, including the Fourth Karma Kuchen, the 10th Palyul throneholder.

relations.subject: Penor Rinpoche
relations.evidence: He trained at the Palyul Monastery in Tibet, studying and receiving teachings from numerous masters and scholars

relations.subject: Penor Rinpoche
relations.role: Third Head of the Nyingma Tradition
relations.evidence: The 3rd Drubwang Padma Norbu, Penor Rinpoche (1932–2009) was requested to become the Third Head of the Nyingma Tradition, and he served from 1993 until retirement in 2003.

relations.subject: Dilgo Khyentse
relations.role: Second Head of the Nyingma Tradition
relations.evidence: Dilgo Khyentse (c. 1910–1991) was requested to become the Second Head of the Nyingma Tradition, and he served from 1987 until his death.

relations.subject: Mindrolling Trichen Rinpoche
relations.role: Fourth Head of the Nyingma Tradition
relations.evidence: Mindrolling Trichen Rinpoche (c. 1930–2008), was requested to become the Fourth Head of the Nyingma Tradition, and he served from 2003 until his death.

relations.subject: Fifth Karma Kuchen
relations.evidence: Penor Rinpoche's students include his "heart sons" the Fifth Karma Kuchen (successor to the Palyul throne)

relations.subject: Fifth Karma Kuchen
relations.evidence: In 2000, Penor Rinpoche designated his successor, and requested the Fifth Karma Kuchen Rinpoche as his successor, to establish his seat at Palyul Monastery in Tibet.

relations.subject: Khentul Gyangkhang Rinpoche

relations.subject: Mugsang Kuchen Rinpoche
relations.evidence: Penor Rinpoche's students include his "heart sons" the Fifth Karma Kuchen (successor to the Palyul throne), Khentul Gyangkhang Rinpoche, and Mugsang Kuchen Rinpoche.
